title: semantic-search-embedset-probe-report
content:
Purpose This is a lightweight probe report and working checklist for onboarding new embedding models / embedsets for semantic search and clustering checks. Goal: provide a fast, repeatable set of checks (quant + qualitative) we run when adding a model or new quantized variant to the model catalog. Focus areas: semantic relevance (search), clustering sanity (cohesion / separation), and multilingual coverage. Quick summary of recommended acceptance thresholds (starting heuristics) - MRR@10 (dev search corpus): >= 0.53 for English generic passage search; expect lower in low-resource languages. - Recall@1 (top-1 relevant doc): >= 0.38 for short-query -> passage mapping. - NDCG@10: improvement over baseline embedding set >= +0.03. - Silhouette score (per-language cluster seeds): > 0.21 for category-balanced micro-clusters. - Cluster label purity (top-1 label match): >= 0.75 on synthetic labeled clusters. - Runtime: embedding encode throughput within 25% of documented perf profile for that model size/quantization. Notes: thresholds are intentionally conservative; we tolerate lower numbers in highly domain-specific or low-data languages but must flag with a documented rationale. Data used for the probe - Core English dev set (approx 5k queries, 100k candidate passages) sampled from internal QA + product help docs. Contains a stratified mix: navigational, transactional, informational. - Multilingual probe (per-language mini-sets): EN, ES, FR, DE, PT, ZH, JA, KO, RU, AR. Each: ~400 queries, ~5k candidate passages. Source: scraped translated help-articles + manual translations for a 200-query core. - Clustering smoke seeds: 12 micro-clusters (approx 20-50 docs each) synthetic + 6 real-world topic clusters from customer corpus (privacy-filtered). - Probe labels: relevance judgments are small-scale human annotations: binary relevant / not relevant and a 3-point graded relevance used for NDCG. Clustering labels are single-topic majority labels. Evaluation steps (scripted pipeline) 1) Encode corpora: run encode_job.sh with batch_size tuned for model. Save vectors using standard naming: -probe-v1-2024-09.
2) Index: build HNSW index with ef_construction=200, M=16 (default). Repro step: save index params file. 3) Search metrics: compute MRR@10, Recall@k (1,5,10), NDCG@10. Comparator: baseline_embed_v2 (our current production small-vocab set). 4) Clustering: run k-means (k = number of seed clusters) and compute silhouette score, purity, and normalized mutual information (NMI). Also compute pairwise cosine distribution plots (visual) for sanity. 5) Multilingual slice: compute delta to baseline per-language. Flag languages with >10% relative drop in MRR or Recall@5. 6) Qualitative spot-check: from top-fail queries sample 20 queries and inspect; annotate common failure modes (stopword bias, name ambiguity, poor cross-language alignment). Quick checklist for running probe (for engineers new to pipeline) - Prepare model artifact (model id, quantization flag). Note: we support fp16, 4bit-gptq, and int8 for some models. - Run encode with tokens_per_batch tuned; verify memory use via nvidia-smi or /proc. - Run eval script: python eval_probe.py --index . --queries queries.json --k 10 --out results/.json - Run cluster checks: python cluster_probe.py --vectors vectors.npy --labels seed_labels.csv --out clusters/-cluster-results.json - Attach artifact links and slack thread to the JIRA ticket. Observed failure modes and quick mitigation ideas - Low recall for navigational queries: often caused by title/URL heavy corpora. Mitigation: add title-aware weighting (concatenate title before passage text) and re-embed. - Cross-lingual drift (ZH/JA embeddings not aligning with EN): check tokenization mismatch and sentencepiece vocab coverage; try re-running with a multilingual encoder or bilingual finetune. - Tight clusters but wrong semantic grouping: could indicate dense lexical overlap dominating meaning (e.g., many docs with same template). Mitigation: use SBERT-style finetune on paraphrase pairs, or add contrastive negatives. - Quantized variant shows lower MRR but similar clustering silhouette: implies nearest-neighbor ranking sensitivity; try hybrid index (add L2 on fp16) or dequantize for re-ranking. Representative prompt / query examples for probe (useful for manual inspection) - English (informational): "how to reset my API key" -> expected: account settings doc, API key rotate guide. - English (navigational): "billing contact" -> expected: billing overview page. - Spanish (ES): "¿cómo restablecer mi llave de API?" -> expected: same as EN reset doc (translated). - Chinese (ZH): "忘记密码如何重置" -> expected: password reset flow doc. - Short ambiguous query: "billing" -> expected: billing overview, invoices page (ranked), not support issue posts. - Long conversational: "I changed my region and now requests fail with 503s, what should I check?" -> expected: region outage page, retry/backoff guidance. - Entity-heavy: "redwood inference ssl cert rotation" -> expected: internal ops doc (note: in public corpora this might not exist; use synthetic entry). Clustering sanity seed examples (short form) - Seed cluster: "payments" -> docs: invoices, credit card update, failed charges, billing policies. - Seed cluster: "model deployment" -> docs: rollout guide, canary steps, rollback. - Seed cluster: "authentication" -> docs: oauth, api keys, mfa, sso. - For each seed cluster we include 8-20 positives, 40 distractors. Expect silhouette > 0.2 and purity > 0.7. Minimal reporting artifact (what to commit to JIRA/Confluence) - CSV of core metrics (MRR, Recall@1/5/10, NDCG) per-language and overall. - Cluster metrics (silhouette, purity, NMI) and top 10 cluster centroids with example docs. - Short list of 10 high-confidence failure cases (query, top-1 returned doc, expected doc id, human note). - Encoding perf (tokens/sec, batch_size used, GPU mem peaks). - Decision: accept / accept-with-conditions / reject. If accept-with-conditions, list remediation tasks and target dates. Notes on multilingual alignment checks - Use bilingual translation pairs to test cross-lingual nearest neighbors: embed EN query and expect the equivalent ES/FR doc to appear in top-5. Report FractionCrossLang@5. - For ZH/JA/KO, include character-normalization checks; small unicode variation can break recall. - For right-to-left languages (AR, HE) verify normalization and direction-insensitive tokenizers. Practical scripts & commands (cheat-sheet) - Encode: ./bin/encode_probe --model-modelid --input corpus.jsonl --out vectors.npy --batch 64 --fp16 - Eval: python -m embedding_evals.search_eval --index idx/ --queries queries.json --judgments qrels.tsv --k 10 --metrics mrr,ndcg,recall - Clustering: python -m embedding_evals.cluster_eval --vectors vectors.npy --seed_labels seed_labels.csv --k 18 --metrics silhouette,purity,nmi - Visualization: python -m embedding_evals.plot_pairwise --vectors vectors.npy --out figs/-pairwise.png Open questions / TODOs - Should we add a synthetic paraphrase augmentation step for low-resource languages? (Sana) -- action: prototype using small translation loop and re-evaluate. - How to automate quantization-aware acceptance criteria? Need a separate regression baseline per quant level. (Marco) - Integration: add a single-circle CI job that runs lightweight probe on any PR that updates embed model list. Scope: run on a 1k-query subset only. (Ethan) Appendix: short example results excerpt (fictional numbers for illustration) Model: openembed-small-v1 Overall MRR@10: 0.571 Recall@1: 0.412 NDCG@10: 0.674 Silhouette (EN seeds): 0.234 CrossLang Fraction@5 (EN->ES/FR): 0.62 / 0.58 Encoding throughput (1x A100-80GB, fp16): 7.8k texts/sec Notes: passes thresholds; minor drop in RU (MRR -12% vs baseline) — needs manual sample check. Contact / ownership - Primary owner: Priya Banerjee (applied-ml) - Probe infra contact: Marco Alvarez (eng infra) - Reviewers: Sana Iqbal, Ethan Moore End of probe report — this is a working doc; add comments inline and push finalized metrics to Confluence page CONFLUENCE-ENG-1234 when ready.
